title: Dispatch surface playback: edge vs core econ memo
content:
TL;DR:
We ran a small set of controlled playback tests to compare dispatch semantics across edge-forward dispatch (short hops to nearby edge cells with small prefetch), core-tiling multiplexing (centralized GPU tiles with larger batching windows), and a hybrid with KV-prefetch evictions. Results show: edge-dispatch-prefetch gives best p50 and p95 for short responses (<=128 tokens) at a modest cost premium; core-tiling-multiplex achieves far better $/1k tokens for long outputs (>=512 tokens) but suffers p99 regressions under bursty arrival; hybrid-evict trades in slightly higher median latency for better p99 and solid $/1k for mid-length responses.

Why we ran this (context):
- Product asks for a short, shareable comparison to inform routing policy defaults for chat-lite vs doc-embed routes.
- We need simple knobs that map to developer-facing toggles: prefer-edge, prefer-core, hybrid-prefetch.
- This is intentionally lightweight — not exhaustive — but focused on practical, explainable deltas to communicate with PM and Console teams.

Experiment setup (short):
- Date: 2026-05-15 to 2026-05-17.
- Hardware: G-core (A100x2) for core tiles; Edge cells running T4-equivalent virtual nodes (quantized runtime).
- Model: open-llm v2-3B (float16 in core, int8 quantized at edge).
- Workloads: 3 synthetic mixes: 
  * Short-burst: 80% <= 64 tok, 20% 128 tok (chat-lite mimic)
  * Mid-thread: 60% 128-256 tok, 40% 256-512 tok (assistant flows)
  * Long-pour: 100% >=512 tok (document summarization)
- Traffic shape: poisson baseline + injected microbursts (10s, 100req/s spikes) to exercise tail behavior.
- Measurement: p50, p95, p99 latency on response-ready (end-of-stream), tokens/sec observed, and computed $/1k tokens using current infra cost model (GPU-hour amortized + infra egress).

Configs tested (names used below):
- edge-dispatch-prefetch: nearest edge cell, small prefetch window (prefetch 16 tokens, KV cache enabled), quantized runtime.
- core-tiling-multiplex: central core fleet, tiling multiplex scheduling, larger batching window (50ms), float16 kernels.
- hybrid-evict: route initial tokens to edge (prefetch 32), then stitch/resume on core if session length > 256 or predicted tail; KV eviction policy to avoid cache thrash.

Raw (annotated) numbers (mid-thread workload, 10k requests each):

Config                    | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | tokens/sec | $/1k tokens
--------------------------|--------|--------|--------|------------|-------------
edge-dispatch-prefetch    | 72     | 180    | 420    | 1,350      | $0.145
core-tiling-multiplex     | 120    | 350    | 1,150  | 3,800      | $0.062
hybrid-evict              | 95     | 240    | 470    | 2,200      | $0.085

Notes on numbers: p99 for core spikes when bursts coincide with long outputs — batching helps throughput but hurts tail. Edge has lower medians due to proximity + quantized runtime but unit cost is higher because T4 nodes have lower utilization and int8 inefficiencies on our current kernels. Hybrid avoids the worst tail by stitching early tokens locally and moving heavy tails to the core when predicted, which balances p99 and $/1k.

Short-burst workload summary (best config per metric):
- p50: edge-dispatch-prefetch (42 ms)
- p95: edge-dispatch-prefetch (112 ms)
- $/1k: core-tiling-multiplex ($0.058) but p95/p99 worse

Long-pour workload summary:
- Core-tiling-multiplex dominates in $/1k and tokens/sec (as expected). p99 improves if burst smoothing is applied (admission control). Edge becomes prohibitively expensive for >512 token outputs.

ASCII latency profile (mid-thread, approximated CDF buckets):
- edge-dispatch-prefetch: [<=100ms: 64%] [<=300ms: 90%] [<=500ms: 98%]
- core-tiling-multiplex: [<=100ms: 28%] [<=300ms: 76%] [<=1000ms: 96%]
- hybrid-evict: [<=100ms: 48%] [<=300ms: 86%] [<=500ms: 97%]

Operational implications and trade-offs:
- Developer UX (chat-lite): prefer-edge gives snappier interactive feel. Cost delta is modest at low scale but compounds at volume. Recommend UI default "prefer-edge" for chat-lite small volumes with an opt-out in Console for cost-conscious teams.
- Enterprise/default: prefer-core or hybrid for high-throughput/long-inference pipelines. Core routing improves unit economics and should be promoted for summarization, batch embeddings, and long-chats.
- SLO design: if customers require p95 < 200ms for chat, edge or hybrid is necessary for short responses; but p99 SLOs need admission control and burst smoothing in core deployment to be viable.

Caveats & open questions (things to follow up):
- Kernel inefficiencies: our quantized int8 kernel on edge shows a per-token penalty for certain attention shapes; rebenchmark after kernel patch (PR #342).
- Network variability: tests used emulated edge latencies; run a small customer-realistic replay to confirm.
- Cost model sensitivity: $/1k uses current amortization assumptions; re-run with alternate GPU pricing (spot vs reserved) for a sensitivity table.
- Stitching overhead: hybrid transition points used a simple heuristic; potential for ML-based tail prediction to reduce unnecessary core handoffs.

Recommended next steps (practical):
1) Share this note with Console + Router owners and ask for A/B of default route for new chat-lite workspaces (2-week experiment).
2) Re-run mid-thread tests after quant kernel patch and with spot pricing assumptions (owner: Evan).
3) Build small visual one-pager for PD and Sales that explains the three knobs (prefer-edge, prefer-core, hybrid-prefetch) with the 3-line summary and a simple cost/latency matrix.
4) Add hybrid handoff telemetry in the onboarding trace (small schema change) to measure handoff rate and end-to-end join latency in real traffic.

Appendix: quick checklist for replicability
- seed traffic generator: scripts/bench/playback_v2 with config: mid-thread.json
- model commit: open-llm/v2-3b@sha:f3a2c4
- runtime flags used: --batch-window-ms=50 (core), --edge-prefetch=16 (edge), --kv-evict=adaptive (hybrid)
- cost calc script: pricing/calc_unit_cost.py --amort=on-demand --include-egress

Notes-to-self (raw):
- push a short slide deck to /product/presentations after Evan's kernel results.
- add a small experiment to try prefetch=64 on edge to see if p99 improves (may hurt p50).
- consider adding 'prefer-core-for-long' automated route: client-side hint + server-side enforcement.

End of memo.

-- Maya
